_comment: Self-hosting dev pack -- REVIEW-ONLY, on a LOCAL model server.
The same slice as config.jichi-dev.json, with one block changed: the
models. Diff the two files -- everything else is identical on purpose, so
the difference between 'a gateway reviews jichi' and 'my own machine
reviews jichi' is exactly the models array and nothing else.
WHY THIS EXISTS. config.jichi-dev.json names an institutional gateway and
three jlu/* models, so a reader outside that institution cannot run the
pack at all -- and the README's own practical response to the measured
latency problem is 'prefer a faster or local reviewer'. This is that
reviewer. It also matches the project's standing rule (CLAUDE.md): local
models, or the institution's gateway; nothing priced.
NO KEY. Local servers need none, so apiKey/apiKeyEnv are absent rather
than empty (docs/LOCAL_MODELS.md). If your server does want one, add
apiKeyEnv and export it -- never the key itself.
THE PORT is LM Studio's default. Change apiBase for the backend you run:
LM Studio   http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1   (as here; docs/BENCH_LOCAL_GPU.md)
llama.cpp   http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1   (docs/LOCAL_MODELS.md)
Ollama      http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1  (docs/LOCAL_MODELS.md)
It is a loopback address deliberately: with no server running you get an
instant connection refused, not a call to somebody else's machine.
THE MODEL NAME must be the id your server serves. Ask the server:
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1/models
or read the list its own UI shows.
The name below is a placeholder that will NOT resolve unmodified.
contextLength MUST match what the server is actually serving PER CLIENT.
An undeclared or over-declared window is the #1 cause of mid-turn HTTP
400s (docs/COMPACTION.md). When in doubt declare LESS -- and note the
trap: a server with parallel slots DIVIDES its context among them. On the
bench this was written against, `lms ps` reported CONTEXT 16384 with
PARALLEL 4, so each client gets about 4096 tokens, not 16384. Read the
per-slot number, not the advertised total (docs/AUTONOMOUS_LOOPS.md).
AND CHECK WHAT THE SERVER CAN ACTUALLY SERVE, which is not what
/v1/models lists: `sh scripts/probe-models.sh <base-url>` walks every
advertised id and reports loads / native / prose per model. Measured
2026-08-21 on a 16 GB ROCm card: five of eight ids failed to load, and the
server log said `unable to allocate ROCm0 buffer` -- the resident 14B model
held 8.99 GB with no TTL, so nothing could be loaded beside it. A full GPU
reports the same way a broken model does: with the card freed, all five
loaded in under eleven seconds and FIVE OF SIX emitted native tool calls.
AND THE PLACEHOLDER BELOW NAMES THE FAMILY THAT DID NOT: on that bench
qwen2.5-coder-14b returned its call as `<tools>{...}</tools>` inside
content, which LM Studio did not translate back, so jichi could not
execute it and doctor --live reported tool calling `text`. The placeholder
deliberately does not resolve -- you must put your own id here -- but do
not assume the biggest local model is the capable one: it was the smallest
that worked. google/gemma-4-12b-qat gave native tool calls at 3,959 MB and
drove a real two-tool turn end to end.
The full measurement is docs/analysis/2026-08-21-local-model-tool-calling.md.
BEFORE YOU TRUST IT, run: jichi --config <this file> doctor --live
That is the one check that matters here: it observes whether the model
emits NATIVE TOOL CALLS (M167). These reviewers work by reading files, so
a model that cannot call a tool cannot review anything -- it will answer
plausibly about a diff it never opened. If doctor reports tool calling
'text' or 'none', use a bigger local model for this job; setting
toolCalling: 'none' makes it an honest Q&A agent instead of a silent
no-op (M149), which is not what this pack needs.
THE EMBED ENTRY IS OPTIONAL. Delete it if your server serves no embedding
model; you lose codebase_search, @docs and auto-context (docs/RAG.md) and
the reviewers still work -- they read the diff, not the index.
_instructions_comment: M516: task rules, loaded on top of the root CLAUDE.md. A review
session needs a rubric that a general session does not, and the
rules block is capped at 32 KB -- so per-task files, not one
_timeouts_comment: Kept identical to the gateway config. A local model on CPU can be slower
than a loaded shared endpoint, not faster -- measure before lowering these
(the pack's README records how that measurement went for the gateway).
_permissions_comment: As the gateway config: headless (-p) has no approval front-end, so the
two spawn tools are pre-approved or /review-diff silently degrades to a
single-agent review. Every agent this pack spawns is readonly: true and
pathFence stays on, so nothing here can write.
